desc: Select a framework and generate the matching CSRF protection configuration code with key security notes in one click.
ui.9: Whichever scheme you choose, combining a CORS whitelist with Origin validation further reduces cross-site risk.
ui.10: The X-Frame-Options / CSP / Referrer-Policy response headers mitigate clickjacking and information leakage.
ui.11: Double-submit Cookie requires the token values in both places to match; attackers cannot read the target site's Cookie, so they cannot forge it.
ui.12: SameSite=Lax is the lowest-cost baseline protection and blocks most cross-site POSTs; use Strict for sensitive sites.
ui.13: csrf_exempt disables protection for the whole view; use it only for stateless callbacks and log it for audit.
ui.14: Reverse-proxy / multi-domain setups must configure the CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS origin whitelist, otherwise validation fails.
ui.15: AJAX requests must carry the X-CSRFToken request header (value from the hidden field), otherwise a 403 is returned.
ui.16: WTF_CSRF_TIME_LIMIT controls the token lifetime (default 3600 seconds); adjust it to your business needs.
ui.17: SECRET_KEY is the basis for token signing; it must be a high-strength random value injected via environment variables.
ui.18: For pure APIs that do not rely on Cookie sessions, consider using token authentication instead of CSRF protection.
ui.19: ignoringRequestMatchers is only for whitelisted stateless callbacks (e.g. webhooks); do not widen the scope.
ui.20: The frontend must keep the X-XSRF-TOKEN request header consistent with the Cookie value (axios can do this automatically).
ui.21: Spring Security 6 enables CSRF validation by default; non-GET requests without a token get a 403.
ui.22: Suitable for decoupled frontend/backend stateless API services; for login-based apps, prefer in-session tokens (csurf).
ui.23: Downside: if the site has XSS, attackers can read the Cookie and forge the request header, so strict output escaping is still required.
ui.24: Set sameSite to Lax or Strict as a second layer of protection; Secure must be enabled in production.
ui.25: The Cookie must have httpOnly:false, otherwise frontend JS cannot read it for the request header.
ui.26: Double-submit Cookie does not rely on session storage: the server only compares the Cookie value with the value in the request header/body.
ui.27: GET requests that change state (e.g. deletion) should be changed to POST/DELETE and included in CSRF validation.
ui.28: All forms (including login and upload) must include the _csrf hidden field; AJAX requests use the X-CSRF-Token request header.
